meta.title: Int. English Tenses (B1-B2) - Indonesian Culture
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English tenses themed around Indonesian culture, combining at least two or more tenses per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined B1-B2 level grammar structures involving multiple English tenses, featuring cultural elements like Batik, Wayang, Borobudur, Rendang, and more.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Batik _____ by UNESCO since 2009, but it _____ in Indonesia for centuries before that.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense ('has been recognized') for an action starting in the past and continuing to the present, with the Past Simple tense ('existed') for a completed state in the past.
explanation.concept: Combining ongoing relevance with completed past states
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + past participle + since + time, but + subject + past simple verb
examples: The temple has been protected since 1990, but it stood alone for centuries.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: While the dalang _____ the wayang kulit last night, a sudden power outage _____ the show.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Continuous tense ('was performing') for an ongoing action in the past, interrupted by a Past Simple action ('interrupted').
explanation.formula: While + subject + was/were + verb-ing, subject + past simple verb
examples: While I was reading, the phone rang.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Rendang _____ the title of the world's most delicious food multiple times, and it _____ a staple at Indonesian weddings.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense ('has won') for repeated past actions with present relevance, and the Present Simple tense ('remains') for a general truth or habitual state.
explanation.concept: Combining past experiences with current facts
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + past participle + multiple times, and + subject + present simple verb
examples: She has visited Bali three times, and she loves it every time.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time archaeologists _____ the full extent of Borobudur in the 19th century, it _____ hidden under volcanic ash for centuries.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Simple tense ('discovered') for a specific past event, and the Past Perfect tense ('had lain') for an action completed before that past event.
explanation.formula: By the time + subject + past simple verb, subject + had + past participle
examples: By the time we arrived, the movie had already started.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense ('will have performed') for an action completed before a future time, and the Present Simple tense ('has') for a general fact.
explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have + past participle, proving that + subject + present simple verb
examples: By tomorrow, I will have finished the report, which shows my dedication.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The musicians _____ the gamelan piece for three hours before the guest _____ at the palace.

explanation.text: This combines the Past Perfect Continuous tense ('had been practicing') to emphasize the duration of an action before another past action, which is in the Past Simple ('arrived').
explanation.formula: Subject + had been + verb-ing + for + time + before + subject + past simple verb
examples: They had been waiting for an hour before the bus came.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('have been studying') for an action starting in the past and continuing to the present, with the Present Simple tense ('remains') for a current state.
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have been + verb-ing + for + time, yet + subject + present simple verb
examples: We have been trying to fix this for days, yet it fails.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: This time tomorrow, the dancers _____ the Tari Kecak at Uluwatu, and the sun _____ behind them.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense ('will be performing') for an action in progress at a specific future time, and the Future Simple tense ('will set') for a subsequent future event.
explanation.concept: Future actions in progress and future events
explanation.formula: This time tomorrow, subject + will be + verb-ing, and + subject + will + base verb
examples: At 8 PM, I will be eating dinner, and my brother will arrive soon after.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The artisan _____ that she _____ the wrong wax temperature, so she _____ the process again.

A.text: has just realized / had been using / is starting

D.text: had realized / had used / is starting

explanation.text: This combines three tenses: Present Perfect ('has just realized') for a recent discovery, Past Perfect Continuous ('had been using') for an ongoing action before that discovery, and Present Continuous ('is starting') for the current resulting action.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect + Past Perfect Continuous + Present Continuous
explanation.concept: Recent discovery of a past ongoing action leading to a present action
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + just + past participle + that + subject + had been + verb-ing, so + subject + is/are + verb-ing
examples: He has just noticed that he had been driving the wrong way, so he is turning around.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

A.text: has celebrated / gained / had been fought

explanation.text: This combines three tenses: Present Perfect ('has celebrated') for an action continuing from the past, Past Simple ('gained') for a specific past event, and Past Perfect Passive ('had been fought') for an action completed before that past event.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect + Past Simple + Past Perfect Passive
explanation.concept: Sequencing multiple past and present-related events
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + past participle + since + subject + past simple verb, which + had been + past participle
examples: We have honored him since he retired, a position he had earned through hard work.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Simple tense ('opens') for a habitual action, and the Present Continuous tense ('is staying') for a temporary situation happening today.
explanation.formula: Usually, subject + present simple verb, but today + subject + is/are + verb-ing
examples: He usually drives to work, but today he is walking.

explanation.formula: While + subject + was/were + verb-ing, subject + past simple verb
examples: While I was cooking, I cut my finger.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('has been raising') to emphasize the duration of an ongoing action, and the Present Perfect tense ('has purchased') for a recently completed action with present relevance.
explanation.concept: Ongoing duration leading to a recent completion
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have been + verb-ing + for + time, and + subject + has/have + past participle
examples: I have been saving money for months, and I have finally bought a car.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Simple tense ('finishes') in a future time clause, and the Future Perfect tense ('will have danced') for an action that will be completed before that future time.
explanation.topic: Present Simple (in time clause) + Future Perfect
explanation.concept: Future completion relative to a future time marker
explanation.formula: By the time + subject + present simple verb, subject + will have + past participle
examples: By the time you arrive, we will have eaten dinner.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The family, which _____ its ancestors for generations, _____ money for years before they _____ the elaborate Rambu Solo ceremony last month.

explanation.text: This combines three tenses: Present Perfect ('has honored') for a tradition continuing to the present, Past Perfect ('had saved') for an action completed before another past action, and Past Simple ('held') for that specific past event.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect + Past Perfect + Past Simple
explanation.concept: Sequencing ongoing traditions with specific past sequences
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have + past participle + for + time, + had + past participle + before + subject + past simple verb
examples: The company, which has existed for decades, had prepared for years before it launched the product.

examples: We are moving houses now, but we will miss this neighborhood.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

explanation.formula: Before + subject + past simple verb, subject + had been + noun/adjective
examples: Before cars became common, horses had been the main transport.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.

explanation.formula: Subject + present simple verb + , a tradition that + subject + has/have + past participle
examples: This recipe contains secret spices, a method chefs have guarded for years.

A.text: will have been observing / will be

explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have been + verb-ing + for + time, and + subject + will be + adjective
examples: By 5 PM, I will have been working for 8 hours, and I will be exhausted.

examples: She had been living there for a decade before she moved.

examples: The software has updated recently, but it still requires a password.

explanation.topic: Past Continuous + Past Simple + Past Perfect
explanation.formula: While + subject + was/were + verb-ing, subject + past simple verb + that + subject + had + past participle

examples: I have just found a coin that dated back to 1800.

examples: Tomorrow, we will launch the website, and currently, the team is testing it.

examples: Every year, the city hosts a festival, an event that has attracted more visitors since 2010.
